name: WCAG 2.1 AA Accessibility Checklist
description: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines compliance criteria for Level AA

categories.title: Perceivable
categories.description: Information and user interface components must be presentable to users in ways they can perceive.

criteria.requirement: Text contrast ratio must be at least 4.5:1 (3:1 for large text)
questions: Does body text have sufficient contrast (4.5:1)?
Does large text have sufficient contrast (3:1)?
Do UI components have sufficient contrast (3:1)?

criteria.requirement: All non-text content must have text alternatives
questions: Do all images have alt text?
Do decorative images have empty alt attributes?
checkpoints: Confirm decorative images marked as such

criteria.requirement: Content can be presented in different ways without losing information
questions: Can content be understood without visual formatting?

criteria.requirement: Make it easier for users to see and hear content
questions: Is color not the only visual means of conveying information?
Can text be resized up to 200% without loss of functionality?
Are images of text avoided when possible?

categories.title: Operable
categories.description: User interface components and navigation must be operable.

criteria.requirement: All functionality must be available from a keyboard
questions: Can all interactive elements be reached via keyboard?
Can users navigate without a mouse?

criteria.requirement: Users have enough time to read and use content
questions: Are users warned before time expires?

criteria.requirement: Content does not cause seizures or physical reactions
questions: Do animations flash less than 3 times per second?

criteria.requirement: Users can navigate, find content, and determine where they are
questions: Are there multiple ways to find pages?
Is the purpose of each link clear?

criteria.requirement: Make it easier for users to operate functionality through various inputs
questions: Are touch targets at least 44x44 pixels?
Can gestures be performed with a single pointer?

categories.title: Understandable
categories.description: Information and the operation of user interface must be understandable.

criteria.requirement: Text content must be readable and understandable
questions: Is the language of the page identified?

criteria.requirement: Web pages appear and operate in predictable ways
questions: Does focus not cause unexpected changes?

criteria.requirement: Help users avoid and correct mistakes
questions: Are input errors identified and described?

categories.title: Robust
categories.description: Content must be robust enough to be interpreted by a wide variety of user agents, including assistive technologies.

criteria.requirement: Maximize compatibility with current and future user agents
questions: Do custom components have proper roles?
